subject: Cardex: secure inference residency confirmation & tech deep-dive ask
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@cardexhealth.com>, Alan Kim <alan.kim@cardexhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Cardex: secure inference residency confirmation & tech deep-dive ask

Marta / Alan — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick post-call recap so we have aligned next steps and open questions. Please correct anything that I’ve misunderstood.

Highlights / confirmed pain points:
- Data residency: all inference input/output must remain in EU regions; no persistent backups exported outside EU.
- Regulatory driver: Cardex needs demonstrable isolation for PHI-adjacent datasets — audit logs and customer-side key control are required.
- Network constraints: customer prefers VPC-based private deployment with outbound egress tightly restricted; potential air-gap to demo environment for initial validation.
- Latency: interactive inference at ~200–400ms p95 is a goal for clinician workflows; capacity will need to handle ~6–8 concurrent sessions during peak.
- Cost sensitivity: Cardex is evaluating tradeoffs between hosted vs dedicated private deployment; control of unit economics is important.

Open technical clarifications we requested during call:
1) Desired cryptographic model: customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) vs Redwood-managed keys?
2) Specific egress rules: is NAT-only egress to a limited set of registry and patch endpoints acceptable, or is fully blocked egress required?
3) Certificate/pinning expectations for mTLS to internal telemetry collectors.
4) Whether SOC2 evidence and network topology can be shared with your compliance team ahead of SOW.

Proposed next steps:
- Schedule 60m technical deep-dive with Cardex infra + security (propose Tue 27 Jun at 10:00 CET). Ben to lead technical agenda and Jasmine to cover deployment packaging and air-gap options.
- Exchange redacted network diagram and typical firewall ACLs (Cardex to share).
- Redwood to share a private-hosting checklist and SOC2 summary (attached).
- Redwood will draft a narrow SOW focused on a pilot (EU-only, dedicated pool, audit logging) for your procurement review.

Attachments: SOC2-summary-stub.pdf (high-level), redwood_private_hosting_checklist.pdf (checklist).

If this matches your read, can someone confirm the list of internal stakeholders we should invite to the technical deep-dive (network/security, procurement, engineering)?

Thanks,
Olga
-- 
Olga Petrov
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai | +44 20 7123 4567
From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@cardexhealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alan Kim <alan.kim@cardexhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 18:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Cardex: secure inference residency confirmation & tech deep-dive ask

Olga — thanks for the clear write-up. Everything below matches our internal notes; a few clarifications from our side: 

- Keys: Cardex will insist on customer-managed keys for the pilot. We operate Azure Key Vault and can provide HSM-backed keys.
- Egress: For the pilot, we require whitelist-only egress. No general NAT egress to arbitrary endpoints. We can provide a short allowlist (registry domains, time sync, package mirrors).
- Air-gap: The initial validation can be an effectively air-gapped environment — connectivity only to a handful of approved endpoints and to our monitoring stack (mTLS).
- Latency: the 200–400ms p95 is aggressive but achievable for short prompts; will track in the pilot.

I’ve attached a brief network outline that shows our intended segmentation and the endpoints we allow for isolated environments (cardex_network_outline.pdf). Procurement will expect a short pilot SOW before we proceed; please flag if you need a PO/contract template from us.

Stakeholders to invite: 
- Network/security: network-eng@cardexhealth.com (they maintain the allowlist and firewall)
- Engineering: Alan Kim (cc)
- Procurement: procurement@cardexhealth.com

We can do Tue 27 Jun 10:00 CET. Confirmed on our side pending your calendar invite.

Regards,
Marta
Marta Ruiz
Head of Product Operations
Cardex Health
marta.ruiz@cardexhealth.com
From: Alan Kim <alan.kim@cardexhealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@cardexhealth.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Jun 2028 08:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Cardex: secure inference residency confirmation & tech deep-dive ask

On Tue, 20 Jun 2028 15:12:00 +0000 Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Open technical clarifications we requested during call:
> 1) Desired cryptographic model: customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) vs Redwood-managed keys?

Two quick technical questions for the deep-dive: 
1) For KMS integration — do you support Azure Key Vault managed HSMs and can you document which operations (encrypt/decrypt, sign) happen inside customer-managed HSM vs Redwood runtime? We need to understand whether keys leave our HSM.
2) For egress allowlist: we use strict DNS-based filtering. Can Redwood provide the minimal FQDN list (and IP ranges if available) that the pilot will require (container registry, model artifact fetch, telemetry endpoints) so we can pre-approve?

Also curious about how Redwood handles automatic fallback if a dedicated pool becomes unavailable (for pilot we cannot allow request routing outside EU).

Thanks — Alan
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@cardexhealth.com>, Alan Kim <alan.kim@cardexhealth.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Jun 2028 14:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Cardex: secure inference residency confirmation & tech deep-dive ask

Marta / Alan — great, thanks for confirming. A few operational clarifications and commitments from Redwood so we’re aligned for Tue 27 Jun 10:00 CET deep-dive: 

Agenda (60m):
- 10m: introduce infra owners + success criteria for pilot (Olga / Marta lead)
- 25m: network & key management (Ben / Alan) — walkthrough of allowlist and KMS integration patterns
- 15m: deployment topology options (Jasmine) — dedicated GPU pool vs VM-isolated pods, caching and latency tradeoffs
- 10m: next steps / SOW timeline and procurement asks (Olga)

What Redwood will provide before the meeting:
- Minimal allowlist FQDNs and optional IP ranges for the pilot (we’ll send as a CSV).
- A short integration note on Azure Key Vault HSM patterns and where keys are used vs persisted.
- A tailored pilot SOW draft (EU-only, audit logging, no automatic cross-region fallback) for procurement review.
- Our private-hosting checklist (attached) as an operations starting point.

Ask from Cardex for the meeting: a single network contact (network-eng@cardexhealth.com) and a point-of-contact from procurement for a quick SOW review. Also please confirm whether you need an NDA prior to exchanging any deeper diagrams.

I’ll send the calendar invite now and attach the checklist & allowlist stub. Looking forward to the deep-dive.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
